title: The Forecast That Moved to 109, Not 130
featured_title: THE FORECAST THAT MOVED TO 109, NOT 130

presentation.challenge: The latest actual demand was 130 units, but exponential smoothing with α=0.30 did not replace the forecast with 130. The next forecast became 109.

practice.topic: Manufacturing, Service, and Other Production Systems
practice.primary_question: How is the next-period forecast calculated using single exponential smoothing?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Setting the next forecast equal to the most recent actual demand and ignoring the smoothing weight applied to the previous forecast.

breadcrumb.name: Manufacturing, Service, and Other Production Systems

case_dna.target_misconception: After observing actual demand of 130 units, the next exponential-smoothing forecast must be 130 units.
case_dna.why_plausible: The latest observation is the newest information, so it can seem natural to replace the old forecast entirely.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: With α=0.30, previous forecast 100, and actual demand 130, the next forecast is 0.30(130)+0.70(100)=109 units.
case_dna.corrected_model: Single exponential smoothing updates the forecast as Fnext=αAcurrent+(1-α)Fcurrent, so the new forecast is a weighted combination unless α=1.

problem_statement: A production planner uses single exponential smoothing. The current-period forecast was 100 units, actual demand was 130 units, and α=0.30. A note sets the next-period forecast directly to 130 units. Determine the correct next-period forecast.

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The latest demand observation was not the entire next forecast.
gates.prompt: How much weight remains on the previous forecast?

options.label: Use Fnext=αA+(1-α)F
options.reason: Single exponential smoothing combines the latest actual value with the previous forecast.

options.label: Set Fnext=A
options.reason: That would be equivalent to α=1, not α=0.30.

options.label: Use Fnext=(1-α)A+αF
options.reason: That reverses the stated weighting convention.

gates.label: Predict
gates.heading: Predict the next-period forecast
gates.prompt: Enter the next forecast in units.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: A smoothing constant below one prevents a full jump to the latest actual value

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the forecasting note
report: C3. Therefore the next forecast is 130 units.

claims.label: C1
claims.reason: This is the stated actual demand.

claims.label: C2
claims.reason: This is the stated smoothing constant.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: It ignores the 70% weight retained on the previous forecast.

evidence_choices.reason: This is the single exponential-smoothing update.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Make the forecast respond more strongly to the latest demand
gates.constraint: Keep the same previous forecast and actual demand, but use α=0.60.

options.label: Forecast remains 109 units
options.reason: Increasing α gives more weight to the latest actual demand.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply exponential smoothing to another period
gates.prompt: If F=200, A=150, and α=0.20, what is Fnext?

options.label: 150 units
options.reason: That ignores smoothing and simply copies the actual value.

gates.explanation: Single exponential smoothing retains a fraction 1-α of the prior forecast.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the forecasting update
gates.confirmation: I confirm that single exponential smoothing combines the latest actual demand with the previous forecast using the stated smoothing constant.

items.label: What failed
items.value: The latest actual demand was copied directly into the next forecast.

items.label: What was missed
items.value: The previous forecast retains weight when α is less than one.

seo.meta_description: Solve FE Industrial & Systems Case E-082: with F=100, A=130, and α=0.30, the next exponential-smoothing forecast is 109 units.
seo.excerpt: Exponential smoothing does not automatically replace a forecast with the latest actual demand. The smoothing constant controls the update size.
seo.direct_answer: Using Fnext=αA+(1-α)F, the next forecast is 0.30(130)+0.70(100)=109 units.

faqs.q: What is the single exponential smoothing formula?

faqs.a: The forecast responds more strongly to the latest actual observation.
